descriptor.name: vendor-lock-in
descriptor.description: Report repository URL references unsupported by GitHub
descriptor.explanation: GitHub Actions accepts repository shorthand in uses. It does not accept full repository URLs. On the github execution target, report URL references in action steps and reusable-workflow calls. An HTTPS github.com URL offers a safe fix that removes its prefix while preserving the repository, action path and ref. Other hosts have no automatic substitution: the same owner/repository name on GitHub does not establish the same action. Docker registry URLs, local actions and dynamic references are excluded. Other execution targets are not restricted by this rule.
descriptor.help: Use owner/repo[/path]@ref for an action hosted in the current GitHub instance. To use an externally hosted action, choose and verify a GitHub mirror, or check out the external source and invoke its local action. The prefix fix is unavailable for URLs with credentials, ports, URL encoding, queries, fragments or invalid shorthand.

examples.description: Remove the GitHub URL prefix without changing the action or its version.
examples.before:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: https://github.com/mlugg/setup-zig@v2
examples.after:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: mlugg/setup-zig@v2

descriptor.name: container-runner
descriptor.description: Report Docker container requirements for selected runners
descriptor.explanation: GitHub-managed job containers, service containers and Docker actions require Linux and a Docker daemon. Report an error for known Windows or macOS selections. Warn for GitHub-hosted ubuntu-slim: it includes Docker client tools but no local daemon; a compatible remote daemon may satisfy the requirement. Inspect available action metadata and expanded composites, with matrix rows and conditions determining which selections can reach the container. Unknown runner facts and unavailable action bodies do not establish a violation. Docker commands in scripts can use remote daemons and are not classified by this rule.
descriptor.help: Select a Linux runner with Docker, such as ubuntu-latest, or guard the container action so incompatible matrix rows do not execute it. For ubuntu-slim, verify any remote daemon configuration before suppressing the warning. Self-hosted Linux runners need an accessible Docker daemon. No automatic fix is offered because changing the runner can change job behavior.

examples.description: Use a Linux runner with Docker for a job container.
examples.before:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    container: alpine:3
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
examples.after:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container: alpine:3
    steps:
      - run: echo ok

descriptor.name: uncancellable-condition
descriptor.description: Review jobs that can continue after cancellation
descriptor.explanation: Opt-in policy for job conditions using always() that can evaluate to true during cancellation. Cleanup and cancellation notifications can require this behavior; the condition alone does not prove a mistake. Step conditions are not reported because action names do not establish whether their work is needed for cleanup. cancel-timeout-minutes does not force cancellation of a job whose condition keeps it running. Warning when enabled; --strict enables this policy as an error, including intentional uses.
descriptor.help: If cancellation should stop the job, use !cancelled(). Keep always() when cancellation cleanup or reporting must run. A standalone always() offers a behavior-changing fix requiring explicit review; compound conditions have no replacement. See [GitHub's always() guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions#always) and the [job-versus-step cancellation test](https://github.com/kjanat/actionlint/actions/runs/41520665123).

examples.description: When this job should stop on cancellation, use !cancelled(). Do not make this change for required cancellation cleanup or reporting.
examples.before:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ always() }}
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
examples.after:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    steps:
      - run: echo ok

descriptor.name: missing-permissions
descriptor.description: Report missing token permission declarations
descriptor.explanation: Report jobs with no permissions declared on the job or workflow. Set require-at to workflow or every-job to require permissions there. An array requires permissions at every listed location. When require-at is omitted, workflows triggered only by workflow_call are skipped. The workflow-call rule compares the caller's permissions with those requested by the called workflow.
descriptor.help: Add permissions on the workflow or on every job. If require-at is configured, add permissions at every location it lists. Use permissions: {} to grant none. See [CodeQL's explanation of missing workflow permissions](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/actions/actions-missing-workflow-permissions/). Set the rule to off to disable it.

examples.description: This job uses no token permissions.

    steps:
      - run: echo ok
examples.after:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo ok

descriptor.help: Check access to the referenced repository and its action.yml or action.yaml.

descriptor.description: Detect untrusted values and secrets interpolated into scripts
descriptor.explanation: Detect untrusted values and secrets interpolated into scripts.
descriptor.help: Pass untrusted values through environment variables or action inputs. For secrets, prefer the tool's native environment variable or stdin over command arguments. GitHub secrets are automatically masked; register generated or fetched secrets with add-mask before use. Masking protects logs, not process arguments.

examples.description: Prefer the tool's native environment variable: GitHub CLI reads GH_TOKEN directly, keeping the secret out of script text and command arguments. GitHub secrets are automatically masked in logs; register generated or fetched secrets with add-mask before use. Masking does not protect process arguments.
examples.before:
# wrong: secret in script text

permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.TOKEN }}" gh api user
examples.after:
# correct: secret in environment variable
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
        run: gh api user

examples.description: When supported, pass secrets through stdin. Bash's printf builtin feeds Docker's password-stdin option without putting the password in Docker's arguments. GitHub masks this stored secret automatically; generated or fetched values must be masked before use. Keep shell tracing disabled.
examples.before:
# wrong: password in command arguments
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      - env:
          REGISTRY_USER: ${{ vars.REGISTRY_USER }}

examples.after:

permissions: {}

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

        env:
          REGISTRY_USER: ${{ vars.REGISTRY_USER }}

descriptor.name: script-interpolation
descriptor.description: Detect template values that may change script syntax
descriptor.explanation: Detect template values that may change script syntax. Unknown strings are checked independently of attacker control. Constrained, nonempty literal strings can be used as shell words; empty and all-decimal strings need a proved data-argument position. Booleans, numeric values, optional matrix members, numeric identifiers, SHA values, and hashFiles results also require that position.
descriptor.help: Pass dynamic values through environment variables and read them as data in the script. Quoting a template expression does not prevent substitution before script parsing.

examples.description: Keep a dynamic value out of generated shell source.

permissions: {}

descriptor.description: Report workflow_run references to unknown repository workflows
descriptor.explanation: Report workflow_run references to unknown repository workflows.
descriptor.help: Use the exact name of an existing workflow in workflows; names are matched independently of filenames.

descriptor.name: syntax-check
descriptor.description: Validate GitHub Actions workflow syntax
descriptor.explanation: Validate GitHub Actions workflow syntax.
descriptor.help: Check the indicated YAML field and its expected GitHub Actions value type.

descriptor.name: inline-suppression
descriptor.description: Validate inline suppression directives
descriptor.explanation: Validate inline suppression directives.
descriptor.help: Use a known rule name and place the directive on the declaration it is intended to suppress.

descriptor.name: unused-suppression
descriptor.description: Report unused inline suppression selectors
descriptor.explanation: Report each inline suppression selector that matches no enabled findings in the checked YAML declaration. Information by default; errors with --strict. A selector used by any analyzed invocation of the same source is considered used. Incomplete analyses do not establish that a selector is unused.
descriptor.help: Run actionlint fix --apply or use the editor quick fix to remove unused selectors. Selectors that suppress findings and the comment's reason are preserved. A suppression comment is removed when all its selectors are unused. Configure lint.rules.correctness.unused-suppression to change its level.

descriptor.name: missing-local-action
descriptor.description: Report local action references that cannot be resolved
descriptor.explanation: Report local action references with no manifest or Dockerfile, a missing directory, or an ambiguous path under case-insensitive lookup.
descriptor.help: Check the uses path and ensure the action has a manifest or Dockerfile. If paths differ only in casing, rename them so each path can be resolved unambiguously.

descriptor.name: string-conditions
descriptor.description: Flag string conditions whose truthiness may be misleading
descriptor.explanation: Flag string conditions whose truthiness may be misleading.
descriptor.help: Use a boolean expression; a nonempty string, including the string false, is truthy.

descriptor.name: join-literal
descriptor.description: Report redundant join calls on string literals
descriptor.explanation: join() accepts a string and returns it unchanged. Context names inside the quotes are literal text and are not evaluated. The separator has no effect on that string. This optional check reports a string literal as the first argument even when the call may be deliberate. Arrays and strings supplied by other expressions are not reported.
descriptor.help: If you meant to use literal text, remove the redundant call. To combine expression values, use format() or pass an array to join(). This rule does not offer an automatic edit.

descriptor.name: collection-comparison
descriptor.description: Detect equality checks between object or array instances
descriptor.explanation: Objects and arrays compare equal only when they are the same instance. Equal contents do not make separately created objects or arrays equal. A condition that grants access or gates a write can therefore evaluate differently from a comparison of contents. This check reports == and != between two known objects or two known arrays. It accepts null checks and repeated access to the same context property, and skips unknown types and expressions that cannot execute.
descriptor.help: Compare the fields or array elements that determine equality. Disable this rule for a deliberate instance-identity comparison.

examples.description: Compare the object properties that matter to the condition.

    steps:
      - run: echo ok
examples.after:

permissions: {}

  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ fromJSON('{"ready":true}').ready == fromJSON('{"ready":true}').ready }}
    steps:
      - run: echo ok

descriptor.name: coercion
descriptor.description: Warn about surprising string and comparison coercions
descriptor.explanation: Warn when a string parameter converts a boolean or null, when a comparison mixes a collection with a type other than null, or when an ordering comparison uses booleans, null or collections. These expressions are valid in GitHub Actions. Unknown types do not establish a suspicious conversion. Collection equality within the same type is allowed because Actions compares instance identity. Equality with null is a presence check and is allowed.
descriptor.help: Check the intended argument or operand type. Use a string literal when text is intended, or compare values of the intended types. This rule offers no automatic edit because the intended value is unknown.

examples.description: Use the boolean value directly when checking branch protection.

Compare the caller's known token permissions with the called workflow's declared job permissions. Cache limits are checked for local calls. The expression-reference rule checks references to workflow outputs.

descriptor.explanation: Validate expression values assigned to workflow fields.

descriptor.name: deprecated-commands
descriptor.description: Report deprecated set-output, save-state, set-env, and add-path commands
descriptor.explanation: Report deprecated set-output, save-state, set-env, and add-path commands.
descriptor.help: Write values to the corresponding quoted GITHUB_OUTPUT, GITHUB_STATE, GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_PATH file.

descriptor.name: errexit-status
descriptor.description: Report Bash status reads that cannot capture a preceding failure
descriptor.explanation:
With Bash errexit enabled, a failing simple command exits before a following $? read. The read can capture success, but cannot capture the preceding failure.

The check uses registered interpreter options and follows literal set changes, groups, subshells and known branches. This warning is opt-in because a success-only read can be intentional.

The check excludes reads within condition tests, AND/OR lists and pipelines, and reads of compound-command results. It skips trap bodies, function bodies and command substitutions. Unknown option values suspend analysis until a known set change. Operations that may replace builtins or install traps stop further analysis in that scope.

The rule is experimental because function calls, command substitution inheritance and dynamic option effects are not modeled. Bash behavior is specified at https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/The-Set-Builtin.html; runner defaults are in actions/runner ScriptHandlerHelpers.cs.
descriptor.help: Capture the failure status in an if condition or an || handler when the script must continue after failure.

examples.description: Capture failure explicitly when the script must continue.

on: push
permissions: {}

  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        run: |
          CHANGED="$(git diff --exit-code)"; EXIT_CODE=$?
examples.after:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        run: |
          CHANGED="$(git diff --exit-code)" || EXIT_CODE=$?

descriptor.name: workflow-command-syntax
descriptor.description: Report malformed runner commands in literal script output
descriptor.explanation:
The runner prints malformed or unknown :: commands as ordinary text. They do not create annotations or apply command effects.

This opt-in warning checks literal echo and printf output in Bash or POSIX shells, print calls in Python, and Write-Host, Write-Output or echo calls in PowerShell. It joins writes into stdout lines, including stop and resume tokens split across writes. Command processing is evaluated separately for each possible execution path. Comments and unused strings do not produce findings.

Registered interpreter settings and literal set changes determine errexit. Known failures and exit commands end execution. The check handles the errexit exceptions for conditions, negation and AND/OR lists. Unsupported commands, dynamic output, loops and complex control flow stop analysis of that path. A pending partial line is checked only at a known end of output. Python and PowerShell scripts are skipped entirely when a statement cannot be parsed by the limited literal-output model.

The rule is experimental because language coverage is partial and command-shaped text may be an intentional example. The syntax and case-insensitive extension list follow actions/runner revision 1ba885c2065fd9be317808ab3fd406f392635cf7, ActionCommand.cs and ActionCommandManager.cs. Extension-specific properties are not validated.
descriptor.help: Use ::name::message or ::name key=value::message with a runner command name. Use stop-commands when intentionally printing command examples.

examples.description: Close the annotation name with two colons.

permissions: {}

      - shell: bash
        run: echo "::notice:Up to date"
examples.after:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        run: echo "::notice::Up to date"

descriptor.name: invalid-output-file
descriptor.description: Check literal writes to GITHUB_OUTPUT
descriptor.explanation: GITHUB_OUTPUT requires NAME=value records or multiline records enclosed by NAME<<delimiter and a matching delimiter. This check combines literal writes from Bash and sh scripts, then validates the complete file. It handles literal echo and printf commands, command groups, and cat or tee with literal text from a here-document or pipe. It skips the script if it contains dynamic values, unsupported commands, variable assignments or control flow. Commands that could redefine these utilities also cause the script to be skipped.
descriptor.help: Write NAME=value for a single-line output. For a multiline output, write NAME<<delimiter, the value, and the matching delimiter.

examples.description: Write the value as a named output.

descriptor.name: numeric-values
descriptor.description: Report numeric values GitHub truncates or that cannot take effect
descriptor.explanation: Report numeric values GitHub truncates toward zero or that cannot take effect, such as a fractional or non-positive max-parallel.
descriptor.help: Set max-parallel to a positive whole number.

examples.description: Write the whole number GitHub uses for max-parallel.
examples.before:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      max-parallel: 1.5
      matrix:
        n: [1, 2]
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
examples.after:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      max-parallel: 1
      matrix:
        n: [1, 2]
    steps:
      - run: echo ok

descriptor.name: empty-triggers
descriptor.description: Report workflows that declare no triggers
descriptor.explanation: Report workflows whose on section is empty. GitHub accepts the workflow, but no event ever starts it.
descriptor.help: Add the events that should start the workflow, or delete the workflow.

examples.description: Declare the events that start the workflow.
examples.before:
on:
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
examples.after:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo ok

descriptor.name: empty-job
descriptor.description: Report jobs without steps
descriptor.explanation: GitHub rejects jobs without steps unless they call a reusable workflow.
descriptor.help: Add steps, call a reusable workflow with uses, or remove the job.

examples.description: Give the job steps to run.
examples.before:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps: []
examples.after:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo ok

descriptor.name: empty-run
descriptor.description: Report steps with an empty run script
descriptor.explanation: Report run steps whose script is empty. GitHub accepts the step, but it runs nothing.
descriptor.help: Write the commands the step should run, or remove the step.

examples.description: Write the commands the step runs.
examples.before:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run:
examples.after:
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo ok

descriptor.name: unpinned-reference
descriptor.description: Require full commit SHAs for actions and workflows, and digests for images
descriptor.explanation: Require full commit SHAs for actions and workflows, and digests for images.
descriptor.help: Pin uses references to a full commit SHA and container images to a digest.

descriptor.name: job-timeout
descriptor.description: Require explicit job timeouts within configured bounds
descriptor.explanation: Require explicit job timeouts within configured bounds.
descriptor.help: Set timeout-minutes on the job within the configured bounds.

descriptor.name: cache-write-untrusted
descriptor.description: Report cache write access granted on low-trust triggers
descriptor.explanation: Report cache write access reachable from low-trust triggers. Untrusted code or input can poison caches consumed by privileged workflows.
descriptor.help: Set cache-mode to read or none, restrict the job with an event guard, or document a reviewed exception with an inline suppression.

descriptor.name: cache-call-unrestricted
descriptor.description: Report reusable workflow calls without explicit cache limits on low-trust triggers
descriptor.explanation: Report reusable workflow calls reachable from low-trust triggers without an explicit cache mode. The called workflow can request cache writes despite the trigger's read-only default.
descriptor.help: Set cache-mode to read or none on the calling job or workflow.

descriptor.name: cache-operation
descriptor.description: Report cache actions blocked by explicit cache access limits
descriptor.explanation: Report cache save or restore operations blocked by an explicit cache mode. GitHub skips the blocked operations.
descriptor.help: Remove the cache step or choose an action and cache mode that allow the intended operation.
